paper.title: Linearized Tensor Renormalization Group Algorithm for Thermodynamics of Quantum Lattice Models

model.name: one-dimensional spin-1/2 XY chain
model.lattice: infinite one-dimensional chain with a two-site unit cell (paper uses N = 2^100)

method.note: The thermal density operator is vectorized into a two-site Gamma-lambda boundary state. Each imaginary-time layer is absorbed and compressed with an ITensors singular-value decomposition; every removed scale factor is accumulated exactly once to recover the free energy. The Jordan-Wigner solution is evaluated independently and used only as the benchmark.

params.name: spin convention
params.why: fixes the energy scale of every plotted quantity
params.risk: using Pauli matrices makes each bilinear four times too large and shifts all temperature features
params.fix: unit-test the two-site matrix element and run the deliberate Pauli mismatch control

params.name: exchange J
params.why: sets the paper's temperature and energy units
params.risk: a different J rescales both axes and prevents a numerical comparison
params.fix: echo J in every cell manifest and compare e0 with -1/pi

params.name: chain and boundary
params.source: paper N = 2^100 with periodic spatial boundary
params.why: removes finite-size effects while matching the paper's thermodynamic limit
params.risk: an open finite chain adds edge and finite-size corrections
params.fix: use the dominant trace-transfer eigenvalue per two-site cell

params.name: inverse-temperature range
params.why: covers both the high-temperature Trotter regime and low-temperature truncation regime
params.risk: stopping early misses the beta=120 accuracy claims and low-temperature heat capacity
params.fix: cell success requires the declared beta_max sample

params.name: Trotter step tau
params.why: the paper identifies tau as the dominant high-temperature error control
params.risk: one tau cannot reveal the paper's ordered error curves
params.fix: plan separate resumable cells for every plotted tau

params.name: retained SVD dimension Dc
params.why: shows low-temperature truncation error and high-temperature saturation
params.risk: small Dc distorts beta=120 while a single large Dc hides the convergence signature
params.fix: plot all three paper dimensions from independent cells

params.name: SVD cutoff
params.source: paper retains a fixed number Dc
params.why: keeps the reproduction's truncation rule aligned with the plotted Dc labels
params.risk: an additional cutoff may silently retain fewer states than the legend claims
params.fix: record the actual retained dimension and ITensors discarded weight

params.name: energy and heat-capacity estimator
params.source: paper permits numerical differentiation of free energy
params.why: one LTRG free-energy run supplies all three requested observables
params.fix: use a uniform beta grid and show the exact analytic curve beside the result

params.name: CPU parallelism
params.why: makes resource use and timings predictable on the available laptop
params.risk: uncontrolled BLAS threading makes timings noisy and competes with normal use
params.fix: set JULIA_NUM_THREADS=1 and OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 in the rerun command

params.name: Fig. 6a Dc label
params.why: the actual curve label is the closest evidence for the data shown
params.risk: following the inconsistent caption would create a curve not named in the panel
params.fix: record the source discrepancy in the report and retain the panel image

scope.label: beginner Track 2, all LTRG targets in Figs. 4-6a

risks: No official LTRG implementation accompanies the paper; the layer update is reimplemented from Eqs. 2-7 and Figs. 1-3.
The paper's free-energy normalization equation is image-extracted, so beta=0 entropy and the exact XY curve are mandatory bookkeeping anchors.
Numerical second derivatives can be noisy near the lowest temperatures; the report will not smooth away a disagreement.
TMRG comparison curves are not regenerated; exact XY thermodynamics is the declared primary benchmark.

observe.quantity: relative error of free energy per site
observe.normalization: relative to the thermodynamic-limit Jordan-Wigner free energy
observe.states: thermal trace over the full spin Hilbert space

figures.expected: Smaller Trotter step lowers the error; at fixed tau=0.05 or 0.02 the Dc=100 and Dc=150 curves nearly coincide, showing that high-temperature error is set by Trotter discretization.

results.why: The error decreases in the paper's Trotter-step order, while the Dc=100 and 150 curves coincide at fixed tau=0.05 and 0.02.
results.wall: 10 min 13 s for the shared seven-cell run
changes: The uv launcher was unavailable; the unchanged XY catalog oracle ran with .venv/bin/python.

figures.plots: low-temperature free-energy error and internal energy
figures.y: free-energy relative error and energy per site

observe.quantity: free energy from log normalization; energy from $\partial(\beta f)/\partial\beta$
observe.normalization: per lattice site; energy error also compared with $e_0=-1/\pi$
observe.states: thermal trace, approaching the ground state as beta grows

figures.expected: Increasing Dc improves the beta=120 result; the paper reports delta f about 7e-6 and relative ground-state-energy error about 1e-4 at Dc=150.

results.why: At Dc=150 the beta=120 free-energy error is below the paper's approximately 7e-6 value, and the ground-energy error reproduces the reported 1e-4 scale.
results.wall: 10 min 13 s for the shared seven-cell run

observe.states: thermal trace over the full spin Hilbert space

figures.expected: The LTRG curves follow the exact broad peak and low-temperature linear decay; Dc=150 remains closest to exact at the lowest temperatures.

numbers.Fig. 6a source conflict: panel legend Dc=150; caption Dc=200; legend followed

results.why: The broad peak is reproduced at the exact position and height, the low-temperature decay remains linear, and Dc=150 is visibly closer to exact than Dc=100 down to T/J=1/120.
